primary_claim: Gemma-2-2B has an internal 'Teacher Axis' representing Socratic pedagogical capability, extracted convergently by two independent methods (cosine similarity ~1.0 across all 26 layers); RLHF/instruction-tuning does not suppress this axis but instead optimizes in a direction geometrically orthogonal to it.

effect.metric: cosine similarity between Teacher Axis and IT-shift vector (format-corrected)
effect.value: +0.029 (Teacher vs IT Shift), +0.041 (Assistant vs IT Shift), -0.004 (Teacher vs Assistant) -- i.e. orthogonal

contradicts_or_qualifies: Own pilot steering result did not replicate at scale: pilot improved Socratic behavior from 15% to 20% vs a 10% random control, but the full n=200 evaluation showed no improvement (baseline/steered both ~6%, random control actually rose to 7.5%)

Initial (chat-template-uncorrected) results showed the Assistant Axis and IT shift as orthogonal, contradicting prior literature documenting they should point in roughly the same direction; resolved by correcting for a format-learning confound
stated_future_work: retry the steering experiment on the instruction-tuned model instead of the base model
combine sub-direction findings with steering (e.g. steer specifically for answer-withholding)
map what direction RLHF does optimize toward (relate to refusal, helpfulness, sentiment)
cross-reference sub-direction component structure across other model families and sizes
generalize beyond K-8 math to other disciplines
limitations_stated: the pressure-turn filter for the capitulation experiment used simple keyword matching, not a rigorous methodology
cannot separate SFT and RLHF effects, since the IT shift vector captures both combined
the full-scale (n=200) steering evaluation was a null result, so causal claims cannot yet be made
quote: I found that RLHF doesn't suppress pedagogical ability but rather optimizes in a direction orthogonal to it.
